articles.title: Netflix Calls Its New AI Discover Feature a 'Test Kitchen' to Tailor Viewers' Recommendations
articles.summary: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide. We’ve all been there; like Clueless’s Cher looking into her closet and exclaiming in dismay that there’s simply ‘nothing to wear,’ there are certainly times when it seems like…
body: Netflix is attempting to help with this conundrum with its latest tool, titled AI Discover. Announced on November 3, 2026, it sits on the top bar of the TV app on the far right. Open it up, and Netflix’s AI will conjure up a few themes to choose from.

The streamer’s example of this includes themes like Outsmart Everyone, Family Scandal Sagas, and Royal Court Intrigue. As told in an explainer on Netflix’s website, some of these themes match “how you want to feel,” the people you’re watching with, or how much time you have, while others are based around your recent watch history or more popular, trending picks.

After choosing one of these themes, Netflix’s AI will bring up similar recommendations, presenting more specific themes until the perfect show or movie arises. And if you’re simply not finding anything interesting, you can refresh your search by choosing ‘Something Different.’

Similar to Netflix’s My List option, you can also hit a ‘Tune Your Recommendations’ button, which sits next to your list and Play. This will let you save a recommendation from the AI, or tell it not to recommend a show you aren’t interested in seeing.
points: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide.

articles.title: Police Mock Car Chase Criminal for Getting Arrested Right Before GTA 6 Release
articles.summary: Police in Derbyshire, UK, are going viral after making a TikTok video mocking a criminal who led them on a car chase, saying the suspect will now miss out on GTA 6’s highly-anticipated launch as a consequence of their actions.
body: The short video, uploaded to TikTok on November 3, shows law enforcement officers from the Derbyshire county constabulary chasing a black van through residential streets as the song ‘Flower in a Hurricane’ from the GTA 6 soundtrack plays.

The video leaned into the Grand Theft Auto series aesthetic; whoever edited the clip put GTA 6’s unmistakable UI over top, giving the criminal a three-star rating, and even included a minimap in the corner of the screen that followed his bungled escape. Eventually, police were able to cut him off and make an arrest.

According to the post’s caption, the incident took place in the town of Ripley. The suspect, 28-year-old Jack Vickrage, has been sentenced to 14 months in prison for “admitting dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, drug-driving, and cannabis possession.”

articles.title: WoW: Forever Shamans Are Protesting Class Changes After Being “Completely Ignored”
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes: Shamans.
body: Developer Blizzard recently released Forever's launch patch notes based on feedback and data accumulated during the beta, resulting in a power spike for all classes and major reworks for classes like Paladin and Rogue. Shamans, too, received some significant changes, most notably the removal of a key Elemental specialization ability, Lava Burst, along with any interactions other abilities had with it.

It's that change, and other changes to specialization-specific abilities like Restoration's Riptide and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon, that have resulted in the WoW Classic Shaman Discord going into lockdown in protest. The entire server, which has around 80,000 members, has been made read-only, with a message declaring the reason for why it took what it described as such a "drastic measure."

"Community feedback gets completely ignored and class fantasies are getting destroyed," the server declared. "With this we intend to give them [Blizzard] a sign and show them that the community is not [happy] with how they approached our beloved class. Give us back our class and spec identities and fantasies."

articles.title: WoW: Forever Won’t Get More Class Balance Changes Any Time Soon
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes, but don't expect any more for at least a month. As detailed in Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard is making some dramatic class changes, including major reworks to Rogue and Paladin talents, in time for…
body: However, don't expect additional changes in the near future. Blizzard said it won't be making significant balance changes until sometime next month.

"With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," Blizzard wrote in its patch notes. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."
Forever's three launch raids will open December 9, meaning there will be a little over a month without class changes. But launch and its subsequent months will just be the beginning, Blizzard said.

"This is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004," Blizzard said.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Is Giving Players A Big Damage Boost For Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is changing in some major ways for launch, with Blizzard revealing classes across the board will deal more damage as it pursues design solutions that better fit in with Forever's combat.
body: In a lengthy developer note attached to Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard outlined its philosophy for its latest version of WoW. It said during the game's nearly month-long beta that it was trying to keep player power in check. That meant every time it gave a class new tools and abilities, it had to tone down others to compensate. Blizzard now thinks that was the wrong approach.

"Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options," Blizzard said. "So over the last two weeks, we've raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher-level creatures to compensate."

In addition to classes simply doing more damage, classes themselves are changing in major ways. Elemental Shamans, for example, have had Lava Burst, a key part of their class during the beta, removed entirely. It's an example of what Blizzard said was the developer hastily "turning to Burning Crusade or Wrath-era solutions" rather than creating new ideas for how classes should play in Forever compared to previous versions of WoW.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever is changing in some major ways for launch, with Blizzard revealing classes across the board will deal more damage as it pursues design solutions that better fit in with…

articles.title: DC Studios Has Officially Cast Its New Robin
articles.summary: DC Studios has multiple Batman and Batman-adjacent projects in the works, like its The Brave and the Bold movie and a Poison Ivy TV series. On the docket for 2028 is Dynamic Duo, an ambitious animated film about two Robins: Dick Grayson and Jason Todd.
body: Co-CEO Peter Safran confirmed who will be starring as one of those Robins. Speaking with Collider, he said How to Train Your Dragon star Mason Thames will play Dick Grayson, DC 's first Boy Wonder who later became the hero Nightwing.
"Mason always wanted to be Dick Grayson," Safran said. "He came in, and auditioned the shit out of it, and was awesome."

Safran's official confirmation comes after Hollywood insiders reported in September that Thames would play Grayson. Other reported cast members are Logan Kim as Jason Todd, Marsai Martin as Barbara Gordon, Lee Pace as Red Hood 1, and Steve Buscemi as Red Hood 2. Dynamic Duo is being directed by Arthur Mintz and will be released on Sept. 22, 2028.

Comic book continuity is a lot to keep up with, and DC Studios' upcoming slate is no different. Recent projects like Superman and Clayface will be part of the DC Universe (DCU), as will The Brave and the Bold. But Matt Reeves and Robert Pattinson's The Batman movies take place in a separate continuity, and are considered Elseworlds stories.
points: DC Studios has multiple Batman and Batman-adjacent projects in the works, like its The Brave and the Bold movie and a Poison Ivy TV series.

articles.title: WoW: Forever's Beta Was Pure Magic. No One Knows What Happens Next
articles.summary: I only took the character to level 6, however. I realized that this was the character I'd want to play and the path I'd want to follow in the live game when it launches this week, on Nov. 4, and I didn't want to spoil that experience.
body: The first thing I did in the World of Warcraft: Forever beta was roll a Troll. It was an instinctive response; my original WoW character, all the way back in 2005, was a Troll, and the sun-baked plains and dustbowls of Durotar and The Barrens will always be my Azerothian homeland. Naturally, the first thing I wanted to see in WoW: Forever 's reimagining of classic WoW was how these environs look in the game's gorgeous new rendering.

I had a nice time. I experimented with the official gamepad support and found it very useful, if not a natural fit for every facet of WoW 's complex interface. I marveled at the developers' ability to write quests and build landscapes in the classic WoW style, effectively unlearning two decades' worth of evolving game design.

Here is an MMO that is simultaneously tougher and more relaxing than the modern game. It's less directed and has a much slower pace. It's dangerous to battle more than two everyday monsters at a time, and you will sometimes dip below 80% health while questing (unthinkable in modern WoW ). This is a game that forces you to take your time, sweat the details, cover ground slowly, and live in the moment.

articles.title: Arc Raiders devs say that using generative AI voice acting was necessary as actors "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"
articles.summary: Developers at Embark Studios, the company behind Arc Raiders, have spoken on the use of generative AI voice acting in the extraction shooter. It's argued that the initial use of generative AI line reads was a benefit to the voice actors, as they: "would just go crazy if they had to read all of…
body: This comes from a recently released video by Embark, focused on Arc Raider's sound and music. In it, several key members of staff speak on the game's use of generative AI, be it the initial use of it for voice lines, and the gradual replacement of it with human line reads.

Audio director Bence Pajor first spoke about the struggles he ran into at previous studios; how gameplay decisions couldn't be changed because voice lines were already locked in. He describes this as a "true pain", and that it places stress on the writing team, dialogue team, and voice actors who may have scheduling clashes. He said that using reachable voice actors in Stockholm, and using the tools available, made life easier for everyone.

Pajor continues by pointing to Arc Raider's many updates and changes since its release in October 2025, it would be impractical to call in voice actors to record lines every time an altered line read needed to happen. Two voice actors present in the video - Jo Rideout (Shani) and Diana Gardner (Celeste) - also shared their feelings on it. Gardner said it was "freeing" that she could take a job somewhere else, without worrying about cancelling other shoots or projects.
points: Developers at Embark Studios, the company behind Arc Raiders, have spoken on the use of generative AI voice acting in the extraction shooter.

The game, which we now know carries the subtitle Sentinel, was revealed in a special video that took place today, 3rd November 2026, almost exactly 15 years since the launch of The Elder Scrolls…
body: In the trailer, a glimpse of the new game - mostly with some fancy sand physics - before the name, Sentinel, is revealed formally. Sands of time scattered by fate," says a quote in the video, attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

"For 40 years, we've explored new worlds, told unforgettable stories, and gone on incredible adventures together," says a blurb for new video. "From everyone at Bethesda Game Studios, thank you for joining us along this journey, for making these worlds your own, and for inspiring us to keep creating. Here's to 40 more."

This reveal comes after a report last week suggested we'd be seeing more of the highly-anticipated fantasy RPG in November, and which also predicted the name of the game. That report suggested that the title will take place in the Tamriel region of Hammerfell, will touch on the "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts".
